autor.portraet_legende: Major-General Sir Charles Edward Callwell, K.C.B., 1859–1928
bio_absaetze: Major-General Sir Charles Edward Callwell belonged to that notable succession of British officers for whom the practice of war and its systematic study formed complementary occupations.

His military writings included Small Wars: Their Principles and Practice, a work of lasting importance in the literature of expeditionary operations, and studies devoted to the influence of sea power upon land campaigns, the conduct of military expeditions and the wider problems of imperial warfare.

During the Great War he served in the higher machinery of British military administration and acquired direct experience of the competing demands placed upon the War Office by a conflict fought upon several continents.
His authority as a biographer arose not merely from rank or literary accomplishment, but from his familiarity with the professional world in which Sir Stanley Maude had been formed.

buch.titel: The Life of Sir Stanley Maude
buch.untertitel: The General Who Restored British Arms in Mesopotamia
buch.reihe: GREEN SERIES · The British Empire Collection
buch.kicker: Lieutenant-General Sir Stanley Maude, K.C.B., C.M.G., D.S.O.
blurb: Sir Stanley Maude is remembered for one city. Callwell’s life of him, written in 1920 by the general who had been Director of Military Operations at the War Office, shows what stood behind it: a Coldstream officer under fire at Suakin in 1885, a brigade-major of Guards on the march to Pretoria, Military Secretary at Ottawa, a staff officer on the Aisne, wounded at St. Eloi, and the commander who took the 13th Division off Helles on the last night of the evacuation.

In Mesopotamia he inherited an army that had lost Kut and the men sent to relieve it. He would not advance until the wharves, the river craft, the railway and the hospitals could carry an advance; then, between December 1916 and March 1917, he took the Turkish lines below Kut one by one, crossed the Tigris at Shumran, forced the Diyala and entered Baghdad. Eight months later he was dead of cholera in the city he had taken.

This edition prints the complete text of 1920 with its photographs and maps, and adds Maude’s appointments and honours from the Gazette, the Order of Battle of the Baghdad campaign, a register of the persons of the book, a glossary and an afterword on the war for the Gulf and the two rivers.
kurzbeschreibung: Major-General Sir Charles Edward Callwell’s 1920 life of Sir Stanley Maude, the general who rebuilt the army in Mesopotamia after Kut and entered Baghdad in March 1917.
From his early service in the Coldstream Guards to his final command upon the Tigris, Maude's career is presented by one of the foremost British military writers of his generation.

The AETERNUS edition preserves the original historical work and adds new studies of the Persian Gulf, imperial strategy, the Indian Army, the operations of 1916–1917 and the enduring military significance of Maude's achievements.
